18.changes: Nothing worth changing — wine keeps the melted raclette loose and the high-heat finish already matches other gratin recipes; no comparable well-reviewed version suggests a better method.

70.changes: Cloudy Kitchen's well-tested puff pastry version freezes twisted straws 15-20 minutes before baking so they hold their twist; this recipe skips that and risks them unwinding in the oven.

110.changes: Nothing worth changing. Shortening-based dough (per King Arthur's own gingersnap) doesn't need chilling to control spread the way butter-based dough would; bake-time control for soft centers is already correct.

114.changes: Stored ingredients/directions are corrupted Google-snippet fragments, missing eggs, butter, milk and salt entirely. Real recipe is Food Network's 'Corn Muffins' (Ina Garten): melted butter not oil, fill cups to the top, bake 30 min at 350F.

115.changes: Nothing worth changing. Technique (chill before slicing) already matches Taste of Home's well-reviewed original; no consistent complaints found about sogginess or filling firmness across 24 reviews.

143.changes: Nothing worth changing. This is Ina's standard fast dredge-and-pan-fry technique, matching how sole meuniere is classically made; no reported failure points, and the dish is already quick.

145.changes: Nothing worth changing. 92 ratings at 4.79 stars with comments limited to glassware and praise; the gin-elderflower-lemon-sparkling ratio is the standard build for this drink.

146.changes: Nothing worth changing. Cook's note already calls it a hit; poaching the diced salmon directly in the hot tomato-cream sauce, as Hazan does, is the standard technique for this dish.

148.changes: Nothing worth changing. Dressing goes onto the farro while still hot and the feta is diced rather than crumbled, both matching best practice for grain tabbouleh; no reported failure points.

149.changes: ATK's benchmark French onion soup blends chicken and beef broth for depth; this uses only chicken. Swap ~2 of 6 cups broth for beef stock, no extra time.

154.changes: Nothing worth changing. Ratio and immediate-unmolding technique already match the most highly-rated versions elsewhere (Mama Gourmand, ATK); browned-butter depth and almond flour crumb are already dialed in.

166.changes: Every well-reviewed crab dip recipe drains and pats the lump crabmeat dry before mixing - this one doesn't, and residual liquid is the top cause of soggy baked crab dishes.

176.changes: Well-reviewed versions (Lebovitz) poke each puff 5 minutes before done to vent steam and prevent soggy centers - this recipe skips that. With two ovens, bake the two sheets separately instead of rotating on shared racks.

184.changes: Your 8/25 note already found this: 30-40/lb shrimp are much smaller than the recipe's 16-20/lb jumbo, so the same 1.5 min/side overcooks them. Cut grill time to ~45 sec/side for smaller shrimp.

190.changes: Nothing worth changing. Your 12/2022 note already confirms this worked great, and it matches King's Hawaiian's own official method - no slit-cutting or resting step found in comparable well-reviewed versions.

230.changes: ATK finds head-on whole fish gives deeper flavor than head/tail-off — likely why this tasted mild. Ask the fishmonger to leave heads on if possible; score the skin for faster, even seasoning.

236.changes: Add a pinch of nutmeg to the cream sauce — nearly every comparable tetrazzini recipe includes it for subtle warmth, and this one omits it. Otherwise matches best practice already.
